title: People ending in -ist
description: Nouns ending in -ist name a person by their views, field or job (Optimist, Journalist, Pianist). As words for male or mixed people they are masculine; the female form adds -in (die Journalistin). Short words that are not people don't follow this rule: die Frist, die List.

exceptions.note: Means deadline, a short native word and not a person, so the -ist person rule doesn't apply.
Means cunning or a trick, not a person, so the -ist person rule doesn't apply.

title: Nouns of more than one syllable ending in -ast
description: Nouns of more than one syllable ending in -ast are masculine, both things (der Kontrast, der Palast) and people (der Enthusiast, der Gymnasiast). One-syllable words are not covered: die Last, die Rast and die Hast are feminine, while der Gast and der Ast are masculine.

exceptions.note: A one-syllable word (load, burden); the rule is for longer -ast nouns.

title: Nouns ending in -ich and -ig
description: Nouns ending in -ich or -ig are almost always masculine (der Teppich, der Kranich, der Essig, der Käfig). Don't confuse -ich with -icht, which is neuter (das Dickicht).

exceptions.note: Brushwood: a rare neuter exception to the -ig rule.

title: Nouns ending in -age
description: Nouns ending in -age, mostly from French and pronounced the French way (-ahsche), are feminine: die Reportage, die Blamage, die Garage.

exceptions.note: An English loanword pronounced the English way; it only ends in -age in spelling and is neuter.

title: Nouns ending in -ade
description: Nouns ending in -ade are feminine: die Fassade, die Blockade, die Parade. Words for people are the exception: der Nomade.

exceptions.note: A word for a person (nomad) and therefore masculine like other male person nouns; a woman is die Nomadin.

title: Nouns ending in -ette
description: Nouns ending in -ette are feminine: die Silhouette, die Etikette, die Tablette. Don't confuse it with -ett without the final e, which is often neuter (das Ballett, das Kabinett).
